note: Set affiliateUrl on an item to turn that name into a link on every crop that lists it. Leave affiliateUrl as an empty string to show the item as plain text.

items.name: Certified seed potatoes
items.detail: Named seed potatoes, not tubers from the supermarket.

items.name: Peat-free seed compost
items.detail: A fine compost for modules and small pots. The RHS recommends peat-free mixes.

items.name: Peat-free multi-purpose compost
items.detail: For pots, modules and containers once seedlings need more body.

items.name: Module trays or small pots
items.detail: For crops started under cover. Deep pots suit peas, beans and sweetcorn.

items.name: Labels
items.detail: Variety and sowing date, so succession sowings do not get mixed up.

items.name: Horticultural fleece
items.detail: For early sowings and for covering tender plants if a late frost is forecast.

items.name: Cloches
items.detail: Useful for warming a row before you sow, and for protecting early carrots and salads.

items.name: Insect-proof mesh
items.detail: The RHS found a full cover is the most effective defence against carrot fly, and it also keeps pigeons and caterpillars off brassicas.

items.name: Canes or hazel poles
items.detail: Runner beans need supports about 2.5m tall. Cordons of tomatoes need a cane or a string.

items.name: Soft twine
items.detail: For tying in tomatoes and beans without cutting the stem.

items.name: Fork
items.detail: For lifting roots and potatoes without spearing the crop.

items.name: Dibber
items.detail: For leek holes about 15cm deep. A trowel handle will do.

items.name: Watering can with a rose
items.detail: A fine rose avoids washing small seed out of the drill.

items.name: High-potassium liquid feed
items.detail: For tomatoes and other container crops once the first fruits start to swell.

items.name: Pots or a growing bag
items.detail: Tomatoes can go one to a 30 to 45cm pot, or two to a standard growing bag.

items.name: Netting
items.detail: Birds pull up new garlic and onion sets, and they take strawberries and sweetcorn.

items.name: Garden compost or well-rotted manure
items.detail: Dug or mulched in before planting. Do not use fresh manure.
